items.quote: Cartesian product of two non-empty sets.
items.text: What you'll learn: the Cartesian product of two non-empty sets.

items.quote: Ordered pair.
A cartesian product.
An arrow diagram.
A cartesian diagram.
Relation.
items.notes: Listed here but taught in Lesson 1-2.

items.quote: Find a set of the ordered pairs which satisfy the relation
items.text: Think and Discuss 1: find the ordered pairs satisfying y = 2x - 1 for x = 0, 1, 2.

items.quote: Represent these ordered pairs graphically
items.text: Think and Discuss 2: plot those pairs in the coordinate plane.

items.quote: Does the ordered pair (3, 5) equal the ordered pair (5, 3)?
items.text: Think and Discuss 3: is (3, 5) equal to (5, 3)? Use the graph.

items.quote: From the previous, we notice:
items.text: Introduces the five points below as conclusions drawn from Think and Discuss.

items.quote: a is called the first projection
items.claim: In the ordered pair (a, b), a is the first projection and b is the second projection.

items.quote: represented by one and only one point
items.claim: Each ordered pair is represented by one and only one point in the coordinate plane.

items.quote: If a ≠ b then ( a , b ) ≠ ( b , a ) , Why?
items.claim: If a ≠ b then (a, b) ≠ (b, a). The book asks why and prints no answer.
An ordered pair is not the set of its two elements.

items.quote: If (a , b) = (x , y) then a = x , b = y
items.claim: Equal ordered pairs have equal first projections and equal second projections.

items.quote: Find x, y if: (x - 2 , 3) = (5, y + 1)
items.stem: Example 1: find x and y if (x - 2, 3) = (5, y + 1).

items.quote: Find a and b in each of the following:
If X = {a , b}, Y = { -1 , 0 , 3) then find
items.stem: Example 2: X = {a, b}, Y = {-1, 0, 3}; find X × Y and Y × X. What do you notice?
solution: Shown again as two tables of first projection × second projection
items.notes: The printed Y has a mismatched bracket: '{ -1 , 0 , 3)'. The solution defines X × Y in words first.

items.quote: When X × Y = Y × X?
items.text: Think: when is X × Y = Y × X?

items.quote: Are the number of elements of X × Y = the number of elements of Y × X?
items.text: Think: do X × Y and Y × X have the same number of elements?

items.quote: X × Y = {(a , b) : a ∈ X , b ∈ Y}
items.claim: For finite non-empty sets X and Y, X × Y is the set of ordered pairs (a, b) with a in X and b in Y.

items.quote: X × Y ≠ Y × X where :X ≠ Y
items.claim: X × Y ≠ Y × X when X ≠ Y.

items.quote: n (X × Y) = n (Y × X) = n (X) × n (Y)
items.claim: The number of elements of the product is the product of the numbers of elements.

items.quote: where n denotes the number of set elements
items.claim: n(X) is the number of elements of the set X.

items.quote: If (k, m) ∈ X × Y then k ∈ X, m ∈ Y
items.claim: A pair in X × Y has its first projection in X and its second in Y.

items.quote: written as X2 and it is read as (X two)
items.claim: X × X = {(a, b) : a, b ∈ X} is written X² and read "X two".

items.quote: represent the sets of X , Y , Z with venn diagram
items.stem: Example 3: X = {1}, Y = {2, 3}, Z = {2, 5, 6}. Draw a Venn diagram, then find products and combinations with union, intersection and difference.

parts.label: Fifth
parts.notes: The book gives Z - Y = {5, 6} and leaves the rest as 'Complete'.

items.notes: Uses union, intersection and set difference from earlier grades.

items.quote: venn diagram
items.caption: Venn diagram of X = {1}, Y = {2, 3}, Z = {2, 5, 6}: Y and Z overlap in {2}; X is separate.

items.quote: The representation of the cartesian product:
items.text: Heading that moves from listing the product to drawing it.

items.quote: If X = {1, 2}, Y {3, 4, 5} Find: X × Y, and represent it
items.stem: Example 4: X = {1, 2}, Y = {3, 4, 5}; find X × Y and represent it by an arrow diagram and by a Cartesian diagram.
solution: Arrow diagram: an arrow from each first projection (in X) to each second projection (in Y)
Cartesian diagram: X horizontal, Y vertical; each intersection point is one ordered pair

items.quote: represents each ordered pair by an arrow that starts from its first projection
items.claim: In an arrow diagram, each ordered pair is an arrow from its first projection to its second projection.

items.quote: the elements of set X is represented horizontally
items.claim: In a Cartesian diagram (perpendicular graphical net), X runs horizontally, Y vertically, and each intersection point is an ordered pair of X × Y.

items.quote: X × Y
items.caption: Arrow diagram and Cartesian diagram of {1, 2} × {3, 4, 5}.

notation.notes: The diagram labels use the Arabic decimal separator as the pair separator.

items.quote: If X = {3, 4 , 8} then find, X × X
items.stem: Example 5: X = {3, 4, 8}; find X × X and draw its arrow diagram.
solution: Pairs with equal projections, (3, 3), (4, 4), (8, 8), are drawn as loops

items.quote: if X is an infinite set
items.claim: If X is infinite, X × X has infinitely many elements.

items.quote: How can you represent the cartesian product of each of the following?
items.text: Think: how can you represent N × N, Z × Z, Q × Q and R × R?
items.notes: The book's own bridge into the infinite products on p.11.

items.quote: To represent the cartesian product of N× N
items.claim: N × N: two perpendicular lines meeting at O, natural numbers marked on each, and the grid of intersection points; each point is one pair of N × N.

items.quote: point A represents the ordered pair (3 , 2)
items.text: A is (3, 2) and B is (0, 4); complete: C is ( , ) and O is ( , ).

parts.label: C
parts.notes: Read from the figure at 200 dpi; verify against the print.

items.quote: This net is known as the coordinat plane of Z×Z
items.claim: Z × Z: integers on both axes, O is (0, 0); the net is the coordinate plane of Z × Z.

items.quote: Identify the ordered pairs which represented by the points A , B , C and D
items.text: Drill: identify the pairs shown by points A, B, C, D on the Z × Z net.

items.quote: To represent the cartesian product Q × Q
items.text: Q × Q: draw the net with rational numbers on both lines and locate A(3, 5/2), B(-3/2, 4), C(-3, -3/2), D(5/2, -3/2).

items.quote: Representing the cartesian product RXR
items.claim: R × R: real numbers on both lines; the horizontal line is the x-axis, the vertical the y-axis; the plane splits into four quadrants.

items.quote: first quadrent x > 0, y > 0
items.claim: Quadrant signs: first x > 0, y > 0; second x < 0, y > 0; third x < 0, y < 0; fourth x > 0, y < 0.

items.quote: tell the quadrant or the axis where each of the following points is located
items.stem: Example 6: for A(3, 3), B(3, -2), C(-4, -2), D(-4, 3), E(0, -3), F(2, 0), give the quadrant or axis.

items.quote: If X = [ - 2 , 3] find the location which represents X × X.
items.text: Drill: X = [-2, 3]. Shade X × X, and say which of A(1, 2), B(3, -1), C(-1, 4), D(-2, 0) belong to it.

learning_objectives.label: Ordered pairs and equality
learning_objectives.description: Determine whether two ordered pairs are equal, and find unknowns from the equality of two ordered pairs.

learning_objectives.label: Cartesian product of finite sets
learning_objectives.description: Find the Cartesian product of two finite non-empty sets, including X², and calculate its number of elements.

learning_objectives.label: Products with set operations
learning_objectives.description: Find Cartesian products of sets combined by union, intersection and difference.

learning_objectives.label: Representing Cartesian products
learning_objectives.description: Represent a Cartesian product by an arrow diagram and by a Cartesian diagram.

learning_objectives.label: Products of infinite sets; the plane
learning_objectives.description: Represent N × N, Z × Z, Q × Q and R × R graphically, read and plot points, and identify the quadrant or axis of a point.
